assumptions: Importers can lawfully authorize supplier outreach and document storage.
A meaningful share of qualifying importers lacks effective supplier-data operations.
Carbon-methodology review can be standardized without excessive professional liability.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Several paid audits with measured supplier response rates and delivery hours, at least one annual managed-service conversion, and a signed referral or data-rights agreement.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Certificate-bearing CBAM makes poor supplier emissions evidence a direct financial problem, sharpening the value of managed provenance operations.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Importers incur current staff, consultant, and certificate costs, though price tolerance and supplier-response performance remain unvalidated.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Upfront onboarding plus annual fees and recurring shipment updates are attractive, but multilingual outreach and carbon-specialist review may keep the model labor-heavy.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Mid-market importers with numerous non-EU suppliers are a coherent beachhead, but the threshold reduces volume and regional account counts are unknown.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Deep supplier-chasing operations could win a narrow segment, yet customs brokers and ESG suites have stronger trusted relationships and can extend down-market.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A permissioned provenance ledger can extend into certificate forecasting, procurement, supplier risk, product footprints, and other supply-chain disclosures.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Validated mappings, response benchmarks, and multilingual playbooks can compound, but access is nonexclusive, consent-dependent, and replaceable.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Hands-on supplier collection addresses work that filing tools may neglect, but there is no measured response-rate, cycle-time, or error advantage.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The 2026 definitive regime converts a former reporting nuisance into immediate certificate and evidence exposure.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Broker and freight-forwarder referrals could scale efficiently, but no agreements exist and these intermediaries may protect the relationship or bundle the work.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A gap audit is a feasible part-time entry, but supplier nonresponse, methodology liability, multilingual operations, and early hiring make full delivery demanding.

highest_value_structural_change: Obtain an embedded referral and workflow position with a customs broker while retaining ownership of the supplier provenance ledger and direct recurring economics.
main_structural_strength: The service attacks a mandatory, recurring, operationally messy input whose quality directly affects certificate expense.
primary_score_limiter: Delivery economics and control depend on non-EU supplier cooperation and broker-mediated customer access, neither of which is validated.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Supplier nonresponse can make delivery uneconomic, and customs brokers may already own both trust and the natural bundling position.
